title: Submersible Borewell Pump

introduction.definition: A submersible borewell pump is a long, slim multistage centrifugal pump coupled directly to a submersible motor below it; the whole unit hangs on the riser pipe inside a borehole. Water enters through the intake screen between motor and pump, is lifted stage by stage, and passes a non-return valve into the riser.
applications: Groundwater supply for towns and villages
key_points: Motor below the pump is cooled by water flowing past it
Many small stages for high head in a narrow bore

classification.configuration: Submersible, multistage, close-coupled motor below pump

introduction.summary: A borehole (well) pump in which both the multistage pump and its electric motor are lowered into the well below the water level and hang from the riser pipe. The sealed, water-filled motor sits at the bottom so water flowing past to the intake cools it; the pump stages above lift water up the riser. A built-in check valve keeps the riser full when the pump stops. No long line shaft is needed, so very deep wells can be served.

what_to_look_for: Water flows up past the motor, cooling it, and enters the intake screen.
Each stage — impeller plus diffuser bowl — adds head as the water rises.
The stages are stacked so the head adds up along the pump.

steps.text: Water flows up past the motor, cooling it, and enters the intake screen.
Each stage — impeller plus diffuser bowl — adds head as the water rises.
The stages are stacked so the head adds up along the pump.
The non-return valve at the top holds the water column when the pump stops.
The submersible motor is oil- or water-filled; its thrust bearing carries the hydraulic down-thrust.
A drop cable along the riser supplies the motor.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Steep head curve; efficiency peak at BEP; the motor needs a minimum flow velocity past it for cooling.

foundation: Well-head plate or discharge head carries the hanging assembly.
alignment: Keep the riser straight; centralisers in deviated wells.
piping: Riser pipe joints tightened to torque; cable clamped to the riser every 3 m or so.
Fit a flow sleeve if the motor sits below the well screen or in a large casing.
commissioning: Measure insulation resistance of motor and cable before and after lowering.
Check rotation by comparing head/flow both ways (three-phase).
Ensure the drawdown level stays above the pump intake.

routine.task: Monitor motor current and voltage balance.

overhaul.task: Pull the pump; inspect impellers and bowls for sand wear.

lubrication: Water-lubricated motor bearings; oil-filled motors per manufacturer.

causes: Very low head at start-up (empty riser)

A submersible borewell pump is a long, slim multistage centrifugal pump coupled directly to a submersible motor below it; the whole unit hangs on the riser pipe inside a borehole.
Water enters through the intake screen between motor and pump, is lifted stage by stage, and passes a non-return valve into the riser.

video_tutorials.title: Submersible Borewell Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Submersible Borewell Pump.
Monitor motor current and voltage balance.
Monitor water level (drawdown).
Measure insulation resistance.
Pull the pump; inspect impellers and bowls for sand wear.
Watch for motor overheating: thermal trips. Common cause: insufficient cooling flow.
Watch for sand wear: falling yield and head. Common cause: poorly developed well.
Watch for up-thrust damage: noise at start. Common cause: very low head at start-up (empty riser).
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

options: By water flowing past the motor to the intake
questions.explanation: A minimum velocity past the motor is required.

questions.question: Where is the motor relative to the pump?
options: Below the pump, in the well
questions.explanation: The motor is at the bottom; water enters between them.

questions.question: What does the non-return valve do?
options: Holds the water column when the pump stops

questions.question: Why are borewell pumps multistage?
options: To fit a narrow bore while producing high head
questions.explanation: Small diameter limits head per stage.
